11144953_10cab52a.text: The orexin neurons are exclusively located in the lateral hypothalamus (LHA), from where they project to nearly all structures in the brain. These neurons synthesize the orexin neuropeptides orexin A and orexin B from a common precursor prepro-orexin

11144953_cf7c60f4.text: Orexin A immunoreactivity (IR) was found in a restricted group of neurons in the postero-lateral hypothalamus from Bregma −1.22 to Bregma −2.54. More specifically, OA positive neurons were found in the lateral hypothalamic area, the dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus, the posterior hypothalamic nucleus and the perifornical area. OA positive neurons were bipolar, fusiform, or multipolar. Many cells showed orexin A positive dendrites

11144953_c7d56362.text: . Orexin neuropeptides (OXA and OXB) are synthetized by a small group of cell bodies localized in the lateral hypothalamus (de Lecea et al., 1998; Sakurai et al., 1998; Peyron et al., 1998), and these cells are known to send their projections to almost all areas of the brain (Peyron et al., 1998)

11144953_43561383.text: . The very first orexin immunoreactive cells were observed in the lateral hypothalamus at postnatal day 11. The number of positive neurons then increased progressively until adulthood.
